calls.head: Skinner’s hold on the Senators won’t last
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Skinner has been a wall against the Senators, well above his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if the Senators finally get to him.
calls.call: If Skinner starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .895 than to his .931 against the Senators.

calls.head: Tilted ice, toward the Jets’ net
calls.body: The Senators have been near the top of the league at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Jets near the bottom. Expect the Senators to spend more of the night in the Jets’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

surprises.head: Ottawa got the good looks
surprises.body: Ottawa’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.4% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.4% and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

story.head: Boucher scores in his NHL debut as the Senators beat the Jets
paras: The first goal of the game would have been Ottawa’s, but it was taken off for goalie interference early in the second. They got it back early in the period, when Drake Batherson officially opened the scoring on the power play. Tyler Boucher scored his first NHL goal in his NHL debut, set up by Thomas Chabot, 58 seconds later to make it 2-0, and that goal turned out to be the winner. Viggo Björck, in his 22nd NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Adam Lowry, midway through the second to get the Jets on the board.

The Senators carried the play, outshooting the Jets 27-21, and got the result to match. Linus Ullmark made 20 saves for the Sens, and Stuart Skinner, who gave up three goals in Chicago in his last start, kept the Jets in it, stopping 25 of 27. The Senators improved to 14-6-2, second in the Atlantic, while the Jets fell to 10-9-3, slipping to sixth in the Central.
